data.text/markdown:
Tori Trades · the trendline bounce, traded (long and short)

This notebook trades the trendline bounce from Tori Trades' video Once you master this strategy, trading becomes EASY on one stock, candle by candle, from a start date (six months before the stock's last 1-minute candle by default) to its last candle. A long trades the upward lines under the lows, a short the downward lines over the highs; each is the mirror of the other. The lines are drawn by the rules of the visual notebook (topdown.py); the trading is bounce.py. Each round goes like this:
  1. Set up. Draw the lines with her top-down analysis (monthly down to the trading chart), using only the candles known at that moment. The higher charts' last candle is still forming, as on a live chart.
  2. Wait for price to come to a line. Long: a candle's low comes within the entry gap of an upward line and the candle closes above it. Short: a candle's high comes within the entry gap of a downward line and the candle closes below it. Enter at the next candle's open, on the line price meets first (the action line). A long and a short signal on the same candle is no trade. A candle that closes beyond a traded line breaks it: set up again. While waiting, the lines are also drawn again at every session's close (the switch below).
  3. Manage. The first stop sits stop room typical candles beyond the action line (below an upward line, above a downward one). Each new swing (a low for a long, a high for a short: the extreme of confirm candles on each side) moves the stop to just beyond that swing, or just beyond the line if the swing lies past it. The stop stays beyond the line and only moves in the trade's favour.
  4. Exit when the stop is hit (at the stop, or at the open if price gaps through it), or when a candle closes more than close break typical candles beyond the line (at the next open). Then set up again and wait.
Money: a $10,000 wallet, all of it in each trade, profits reinvested; a short is sold for the wallet's worth and bought back. Costs are the repo's: $0.005 a share with a $1 minimum, half the 2 bp spread and 1 bp slippage, on every order. The hurdle is buying the same stock at the first traded open and holding it to the end. The session refresh. Taken literally, "draw the lines after each trade and wait" makes the lines go stale. On NOW from 2026-04-16, the upward lines drawn after the April trade lay near $82. Price rallied to $149 without coming back, so the long-only replay waited five months and the rally's own, steeper lines were never drawn. Switch the refresh off to see that version. Placebo shift moves every line toward price (negative: away). If her lines mark something real, moved lines should trade worse. Two filters are off by default. The trend filter takes a long only above, and a short only below, an N-session daily average. The shortest line traded skips lines whose points A and B lie fewer sessions apart. What 21 stocks said (study.py, 2026-03-30 to 2026-09-29, README): at these defaults every mode lost (long −9%, short −5%, both −8% a stock over six months, against +20% for buy-and-hold). No setting of the entry gap, stop room or close break made either side profitable, and lines moved off hers did no worse. The filters only trade less; they do not trade better.

The trade
The lines

2 · Every trade on the chart

Each trade's action line runs from the candle that signalled to the exit: blue for a long, orange for a short. Triangles are entries, pointing the trade's way; crosses are exits (green with a profit, red with a loss); amber is the stop at every close. Zoom in with the mouse; hover over an entry or an exit for the trade.

3 · One trade up close

Pick a trade (the first one by default). The chart shows the history before the moment the lines were drawn (the dotted line; the slider sets how much) and every line drawn at that moment: upward lines blue, downward lines orange, each with the candles that fixed it: ◆ point A where the ray starts, ★ the candle that stopped the ray (its angle), ◇ point B, the latest touch, where the next line starts. Over them: the band where a low (high) is a signal, the action line (thick), the signal candle, the entry, the stop at every close and the exit. Hover over a line or a point for its details.

Trade 2 (short). The lines were drawn at 2026-04-21 15:45 (waiting: again at the session's close): 2 upward and 3 downward line(s), all on the chart (the thin lines). At 2026-04-22 09:45 the candle's high came within 0.13 of the downward line drawn on the 15-minute chart (point A 2025-12-12 15:45 at 173.70) and the candle closed below it: sold short at the next open, 2026-04-22 10:00 at 103.51, first stop 104.02 (0.51 away: 1 R). The stop was hit: 2026-04-22 10:15 at 104.02, -1.00 R, -0.55% after costs, 2 candles.
